detections.evidence_quote: as soon as you raise your blood sugar, raise your glucose, and you raise your insulin, now your body can't burn fat
detections.summary: Insulin-blocks-fat-burning mechanism offered to explain why mixing carbs with a high-fat diet raises triglycerides.

detections.evidence_quote: you don't need a lot of white flour, white rice, white bread, white pasta.
detections.summary: Hosts describe eating clean, limiting white flour, rice, bread and pasta and avoiding enriched or fortified versions.

detections.evidence_quote: And what I found is that at lunch I wouldn't be craving a Snickers bar, and at dinner, after I ate dinner, I wasn't craving Haagen-Dazs.
detections.summary: Host recounts quitting sugar, losing cravings for sweets after a seven-to-ten-day withdrawal, then craving salty snacks instead.

detections.evidence_quote: And all it took was it was like a seven to ten day period.
detections.summary: Host's own experience of quitting sugar is used to generalize that sugar withdrawal lasts about a week and then cravings end.

detections.evidence_quote: it's a period where you go through the withdrawal and then you're fine.
detections.summary: Co-host frames quitting sugar as going through withdrawal, implying drug-like sugar addiction.

detections.evidence_quote: But they didn't have seed oils. It was like avocado oil.
detections.summary: Hosts blame seed oils in chips and praise a chip brand made with avocado oil instead of seed oils.

detections.evidence_quote: Once I got chips out, I think that that it really came down. Chips, the seed oils, yeah.
detections.summary: Cutting chips is credited to removing seed oils, and a seed-oil-free chip is singled out as the acceptable one, implying seed oils are harmful.

detections.evidence_quote: you make you make really healthy salads with lots of stuff in them.
detections.summary: Host describes making meal salads with avocado, chicken, nuts and hemp seeds, called really healthy.

detections.evidence_quote: we know now through peer-reviewed, published clinical studies that no amount of alcohol is good for you.

detections.evidence_quote: we know now through peer-reviewed, published clinical studies
detections.summary: Unidentified peer-reviewed clinical studies are invoked as settling that no alcohol is good for you.

detections.evidence_quote: A glass of wine a day keeps the doctor away. It's absolutely not true.
detections.summary: Speaker debunks the saying that a glass of wine a day keeps the doctor away.

detections.evidence_quote: you can get resveratrol through supplementation now in much higher concentrations and much more bioavailable
detections.summary: Resveratrol in wine is said to be better obtained from supplements at higher, more bioavailable doses.

detections.evidence_quote: acetaldehyde, which is a poison and poisons your brain
detections.summary: Alcohol's metabolite acetaldehyde is cast as a poison that poisons the brain.

detections.evidence_quote: alcohol converts into something called acetaldehyde, which is a poison and poisons your brain.
detections.summary: Alcohol's harm is explained via conversion to acetaldehyde and acidification of blood pH.

detections.evidence_quote: So, when we shift slightly to becoming more acidic, this is the state where we don't feel well.
detections.summary: Speaker says alcohol acidifies the body, shifting blood pH, and that a more acidic state is why we feel unwell.

detections.evidence_quote: Yeah, you have to skip the sugar part.

verification_candidates.claim_text: Raising blood glucose and insulin stops the body from burning fat.
verification_candidates.evidence_quote: you raise your insulin, now your body can't burn fat
verification_candidates.rationale: Physiological mechanism claim underpinning dietary advice.

verification_candidates.claim_text: Raising blood sugar and insulin while eating a high-fat keto diet causes triglycerides and VLDL cholesterol to skyrocket.
verification_candidates.evidence_quote: Your triglycerides skyrocket. You will see that your dangerous cholesterols, your VLDL cholesterols, will skyrocket.
verification_candidates.rationale: Specific lipid-risk claim about breaking a ketogenic diet.

verification_candidates.claim_text: Quitting sugar brings a withdrawal period of about seven to ten days, after which sugar cravings go away.
verification_candidates.evidence_quote: Oh yeah, it's a period where you go through the withdrawal and then you're fine.
verification_candidates.rationale: Generalized claim of sugar withdrawal implies addiction-like effects.

verification_candidates.claim_text: No amount of alcohol is good for you.
verification_candidates.evidence_quote: we know now through peer-reviewed, published clinical studies that no amount of alcohol is good for you.
verification_candidates.rationale: Broad safety claim about any alcohol intake that shapes drinking decisions.

verification_candidates.claim_text: Drinking a glass of wine a day keeps people healthy (keeps the doctor away).
verification_candidates.evidence_quote: A glass of wine a day keeps the doctor away. It's absolutely not true.
verification_candidates.rationale: Rebutted claim of a health benefit from daily wine.

verification_candidates.claim_text: Resveratrol supplements provide much higher concentrations of resveratrol, in a more bioavailable form, than wine does.
verification_candidates.evidence_quote: There's resveratrol in wine, but you can get resveratrol through supplementation now in much higher concentrations and much more bioavailable.
verification_candidates.rationale: Comparative bioavailability claim that steers people toward supplements.

verification_candidates.claim_text: Alcohol is converted in the body into acetaldehyde, a poison that poisons the brain.
verification_candidates.evidence_quote: alcohol converts into something called acetaldehyde, which is a poison and poisons your brain.
verification_candidates.rationale: Mechanistic toxicity claim about alcohol metabolism.

verification_candidates.claim_text: Alcohol makes the body acidic and can shift blood pH by several tenths of a point.
verification_candidates.evidence_quote: It makes your body acidic, so it actually can move the pH. Of your blood, several tenths of a point.
verification_candidates.rationale: Specific physiological claim about blood pH that is checkable.

verification_candidates.claim_text: The normal range of blood pH is very narrow, about four or five tenths of a point.
verification_candidates.evidence_quote: the pH range of the blood is very narrow; it's only about four or five tenths of a point.
verification_candidates.rationale: Numeric physiological claim used to make the acidity argument plausible.

verification_candidates.claim_text: A slight shift of blood pH toward acidic is the state in which people feel unwell.
verification_candidates.evidence_quote: So, when we shift slightly to becoming more acidic, this is the state where we don't feel well.
verification_candidates.rationale: Acid-body explanation of malaise is a contested health claim.

verification_candidates.claim_text: Agave-based alcohols such as tequila convert to sugar and acetaldehyde more slowly than any other alcohol.
verification_candidates.evidence_quote: if we look at what alcohols convert the slowest to both sugar and to acetaldehyde, by far, agave-based alcohols, tequila, are way out in front.
verification_candidates.rationale: Comparative metabolic claim that steers drink choice.

verification_candidates.claim_text: Sugary margaritas are a recipe for a hangover.
verification_candidates.evidence_quote: That's the part that people are like, "Oh, so I can have margaritas?" No, that's like a recipe for a hangover.
verification_candidates.rationale: Claim that added sugar worsens hangovers is checkable.

verification_candidates.claim_text: After tequila, clear spirits like vodka and gin convert next slowest, followed by full-bodied red wines, with white wines, prosecco and high-sugar wines worst.
verification_candidates.evidence_quote: then you get the clear alcohols, like vodka and like vodkas and gins, and then there's another gap
verification_candidates.rationale: Ranking of alcoholic drinks by metabolic harm is checkable and guides choices.
